meta.priceDisclaimer: Unit costs shown are internal planning estimates, not quotes from Business Edge. Confirm every price and the setup charge with the supplier before committing budget.

1.label: Tier 1 · Walk-up
1.blurb: Hand to anyone who stops. Cheap enough that 200 units doesn't hurt, good enough that it isn't insulting. Target roughly $1.50–$4 landed.

2.label: Tier 2 · Real conversation
2.blurb: For someone who scanned, asked a question, or stood at the booth for more than a minute. This is where the money is best spent — the sweet spot for 'useful, not junk'.

3.label: Tier 3 · Qualified lead
3.blurb: Twenty units, kept under the counter, handed over after a real conversation with someone who matters. Perceived value should read at 2–3× what you paid.

items.name: Microfiber screen cloth in a pouch
items.supplierProductName: Ultra Opper Fiber® Microfiber Cloth in Vinyl Pouch, Full Colour 6"×6"
items.whyItWorks: Weighs nothing, costs nothing, and gets used every single day by anyone with glasses, a phone, or a laptop. The highest use-per-dollar item on this whole list.
items.decoration: Full-colour dye sublimation on the cloth — you get the entire surface, not a tiny logo box.
items.watchOut: Ask for 250gsm+ suede-finish. Their cheaper bulk version (Synthetix, no pouch) drops the price but the pouch is what makes it feel like a product.

items.name: Aluminium luggage tag
items.whyItWorks: Trade show crowd flies. A tag lives on the bag for years and gets seen at every carousel — and unlike a keychain it has an actual job.
items.decoration: Laser engrave. It never wears off, and engraved metal reads as more expensive than it is.
items.watchOut: Confirm the strap type — insist on a steel cable loop, not an elastic band. Those snap in the first month.

items.name: Adhesive silicone phone card wallet
items.supplierProductName: Silicone Adhesive Card Holder for Phone Back
items.whyItWorks: Sticks to the back of a phone and holds a transit card or hotel key. Once it's on, it's on for the life of the case — and it's visible every time they pull out their phone.
items.decoration: Pad print or debossed silicone.
items.watchOut: Confirm it's 3M adhesive. Off-brand adhesive lets go in a week and takes your brand with it.

items.name: Enamel lapel pin
items.whyItWorks: The one category where people will actively ask for a second one — if the art is good. This is a design spend, not a product spend.
items.decoration: Soft enamel at this price; hard enamel costs more but holds finer detail and feels better.
items.watchOut: Only works if the artwork is genuinely nice. A logo on a circle is not a pin; it's a button nobody wears.

items.name: Webcam privacy cover
items.whyItWorks: Sticks on a laptop lid and stays there for the life of the machine. Every video call is an impression — including calls with their whole team.
items.decoration: Laser engrave or pad print on the slider face.
items.watchOut: Ask for the thickness spec in writing. Over ~0.8mm and it stops the laptop closing flush, which means it gets peeled off.

items.name: Retractable gel pen
items.supplierProductName: Zebra Sarasa Dry X-20 Retractable Gel Pen with Rubber Grip
items.whyItWorks: Pens still work — but only good ones. A branded Zebra gel writes smoothly, gets kept, and gets stolen by coworkers. A scratchy stick pen actively damages the impression.
items.decoration: Pad print or wrap.
items.watchOut: Do not let anyone talk you into the $0.59 pen to stretch the budget. That saving is the whole point of failure.

items.name: Bottle-opener card (wallet-size)
items.whyItWorks: Flat as a credit card, lives in a wallet, and doubles as your business card. High novelty on the floor, real utility afterward.
items.decoration: Laser engrave.
items.watchOut: Their multi-tool search mostly returns tape measures — if you want screwdriver/ruler functions too, ask Bei specifically for a multi-tool card, not a bottle opener.

items.name: Lip balm
items.whyItWorks: Consumable = no clutter guilt, so nobody refuses it. Convention centres are bone dry and this genuinely gets used before the show ends.
items.decoration: Full-wrap label — the whole surface is yours.
items.watchOut: Note this one is explicitly non-SPF, and their SPF-15 option is flagged US-only. If you want SPF for a Canadian show, Bei needs to source a version with an NPN.

items.name: Self-adhesive cable organizer
items.whyItWorks: Anyone who travels with a laptop has a bag full of tangled cables. Small, dull, and used constantly — the definition of good swag.
items.decoration: Deboss or silkscreen.
items.watchOut: Ask for a set of two or three. A single strap feels like an offcut; a 3-pack feels like a product.

items.name: Custom knit crew socks
items.supplierProductName: Custom Dress Crew Socks (Made in America)
items.whyItWorks: The most requested swag item going, and for good reason — everyone wears socks, they roll down to nothing in a bag, and the logo is knitted into the fabric so it never cracks or peels.
items.decoration: Knit-in jacquard, not print. Print on socks looks cheap after one wash.
items.watchOut: Confirm the minimum — custom knit socks often start at 288 pairs, which is right at the top of your range. Also ask whether they'll split M/L sizing.

items.name: Dual retractable charging cable
items.whyItWorks: Solves the exact problem people have at a trade show, on the day. Fits a pocket, gets thrown in a bag, and stays there as the emergency backup cable forever.
items.decoration: Pad print or laser on the housing.
items.watchOut: Confirm it carries data and at least 20W, and that the USB-C tip is real USB-C. Cheap retractables are charge-only and slow — people notice. Their TerraTone 3-in-1 is the alternative if you want three tips.

items.name: Magnetic MagSafe-style phone wallet
items.whyItWorks: Snaps to the back of a phone, and the better versions fold out into a kickstand. Currently the highest-perceived-value item at this price — it reads as a $30 accessory.
items.decoration: Deboss on vegan leather, or pad print.
items.watchOut: Magnet strength is where cheap units fail. Ask for the magnet grade and shake-test a sample before committing.

items.name: Foldable ripstop tote
items.supplierProductName: Boulevard Foldable Ripstop Tote with Cinch Cord Handles
items.whyItWorks: The one bag worth giving. It packs down to nothing, so it lives in a purse or glovebox and gets used for groceries — unlike the canvas tote it replaces.
items.decoration: Silkscreen or full-colour transfer.
items.watchOut: Check the seams. Unlined ripstop without taped seams tears on the first heavy load, and then it's a bad memory of your brand.

items.name: Softcover journal
items.whyItWorks: Opened daily for months, which is more brand exposure than almost anything else here. Works because it's slim — padded hardcovers are too heavy to carry and end up in a drawer.
items.decoration: Blind deboss on the cover. Much classier than print, and it's what makes it look like a bookshop notebook.
items.watchOut: Ask for the page count and whether it lies flat. And keep the logo small — a giant mark on the cover is what turns a notebook into swag.

items.name: Mirror sport sunglasses
items.supplierProductName: Sport Viper Mirror Sunglasses w/ 1-Colour Lens Imprint
items.whyItWorks: One of the few items people put on immediately, at the booth — free walking advertising for the rest of the show. Good for spring/summer outdoor events.
items.decoration: Pad print on the temple arm. Skip the lens imprint — people scrape it off.
items.watchOut: Confirm genuine UV400. Also a seasonal bet: dead weight at a February show.

items.name: Blue-light blocking glasses
items.supplierProductName: Blue Light Blocking Retro Glasses w/ 1-Colour Imprint
items.whyItWorks: Reads as a wellness gift rather than swag. Screen-heavy audiences — tech, finance, design — take these seriously and keep them at the desk.
items.decoration: Pad print on the arm, small.
items.watchOut: Don't make medical claims in your copy. 'Filters blue light,' not 'prevents eye strain.' Ask whether a case is included; without one they get scratched and binned.

items.name: Recycled knit beanie
items.whyItWorks: For any Canadian show from October to March this outperforms every cap. Squashes flat in a bag, gets worn daily for five months of the year — and the recycled angle is an easy talking point.
items.decoration: Woven label or small embroidered patch on the cuff.
items.watchOut: Fully seasonal. Great in Toronto in November, useless in Vegas in June. The pom is polarising — ask if there's a plain version.

items.name: Microfiber golf towel
items.whyItWorks: Ends up clipped to a gym bag or golf bag, which is a lot of repeat visibility for the money. Quietly one of the highest-retention mid-tier items.
items.decoration: Full-colour sublimation.
items.watchOut: Ask for the GSM. Waffle-weave at 400gsm+ absorbs; the thin ones don't, and get thrown out.

items.name: USB wall charger
items.whyItWorks: Everyone needs a second charger for the travel bag, and almost nobody gets around to buying one. High utility, and it stays plugged in at a bedside for years.
items.decoration: Pad print on the body.
items.watchOut: Non-negotiable: cUL or CSA certification for Canada — ask for the certificate number, not a reassurance. Also confirm it's 20W+ USB-C, not a 5W USB-A relic.

items.name: Mini maple syrup
items.whyItWorks: The item for people who visibly don't want more stuff — and it's a genuinely nice thing for an international attendee to take home from a Canadian show. Zero clutter guilt, high charm.
items.decoration: Custom label on the bottle.
items.watchOut: Glass and liquid: heavier to ship, and a US attendee flying carry-on can't take much liquid. Fine for a Canadian audience, awkward for a fly-in crowd.

items.name: Wireless power bank
items.whyItWorks: Charges by sticking to the back of the phone with no cable — the version people actually use rather than leave at home. Solves the single most common problem at a conference.
items.decoration: Laser or pad print on the flat face.
items.watchOut: 2,000mAh is under half a phone charge — thin, but people notice. Ask Bei for a 5,000mAh magnetic option instead. Also: lithium air-freight needs UN38.3 paperwork, so order early.

items.name: Find My luggage tracker
items.supplierProductName: Echo Luggage Tag with Apple Find My
items.whyItWorks: Genuinely Apple Find My certified, not a clone that needs its own app. Goes straight onto a suitcase and stays there for years — very high perceived value, and a natural conversation piece at the booth.
items.decoration: Laser engrave.
items.watchOut: Apple-ecosystem only. If your audience skews Android, ask whether there's a Google Find My Device equivalent before you commit the budget.

items.name: RFID card holder
items.whyItWorks: A daily-carry object, which is the highest tier of swag there is. Understated enough that a senior person will actually use it.
items.decoration: Blind deboss only. A printed logo on leather looks like a giveaway; a debossed one looks like a gift.
items.watchOut: Ask what the material actually is. Split-leather sold as 'genuine leather' cracks within a year and undoes the whole effect — full-grain or a good microfibre PU is what you want.

items.name: Folding phone stand
items.whyItWorks: Folds to the size of a deck of cards, gets unfolded on every flight and hotel desk. Feels engineered, which is the point at this tier.
items.decoration: Laser engrave on the base.
items.watchOut: Test the hinge on a sample. The cheap ones go floppy after a month and then it's a paperweight.

items.name: Insulated bottle
items.whyItWorks: The one bulky exception, and only for qualified leads. Worth it mainly if you can co-brand with a name people recognise — a known brand borrows a quality reputation your logo can't.
items.decoration: Laser or wrap.
items.watchOut: This is Bei's generic line. Ask specifically whether they carry CamelBak, Corkcicle or similar — the co-brand is most of the value here. And offer to ship it to the lead's office rather than hand it over at the booth.
